response: Yes, the stretch-sensitive KCNQ1 mutation is a link between genetic and environmental factors in the pathogenesis of atrial fibrillation. This mutation affects the KCNQ1 gene, which codes for a subunit of the potassium channel. The mutation makes the channel more sensitive to mechanical stretch, which can be caused by conditions such as high blood pressure, heart valve problems, or other cardiac diseases. When the heart is stretched, the mutated channel can lead to abnormal electrical activity, increasing the risk of atrial fibrillation. This highlights the interplay between genetic predisposition (the KCNQ1 mutation) and environmental factors (mechanical stretch due to various heart conditions) in the development of atrial fibrillation.
